cases.title: The starter about AI agents
cases.question: How does Brad ship with AI agents?
cases.answer: Brad runs VINDecoded as a one-person engineering team, and AI agents write most of the code. From June 13 to October 28, 2026, 1,235 pull requests merged into its monorepo, and 1,028 of them (83%) came from agent branches in Claude Code and Codex. The essay says the agents are not the interesting part. The system around them is: docs every agent reads before it starts, one isolated checkout per agent, tests the coding agent can't rewrite, a second agent that reviews its work, a gate and a kill switch on every new feature, and one audited door to production.

cases.title: From the essay: features ship dark
cases.question: In Brad’s essay, how do new features reach customers?
cases.answer: New features reach customers in steps, and most merge turned off. Most new features reach production turned off, so merging and deploying code doesn't change what customers see. Turning it on is a separate, deliberate step that takes effect in seconds and can be undone the same way. The steps are: merged dark. The code ships behind a gate that is off for everyone. Next, Brad switches it on for Brad's own account in production through a per-user override. Then one command through the production-task CLI turns the gate on, for example `prod-task shop-ai:on`. Finally, every live feature keeps a named off switch, such as `prod-task shop-ai:off`, and AGENTS.md lists it beside the feature.
